name: C01 cellLabelValue: the double quote is the wrong character
why: a double-quoted value is read from its quote: the quote becomes the id's first character and the id is empty

name: C02 cellLabelValue: the single quote is the wrong character
why: a single-quoted value is read from its quote

name: C03 cellLabelValue: the single quote skips two characters
why: the id of a single-quoted value loses its first character

name: C04 cellLabelValue: a quote only when both quotes are there at once
why: no value is ever quoted

name: C05 cellLabelValue: a colon may start the id
why: `:x` is read as an id; the pattern refused it

name: C06 cellLabelValue: a dot may start the id
why: `.x` is read as an id; the pattern refused it

name: C07 cellLabelValue: a dash may start the id
why: `-x` and a quoted `"-a"` are read as ids; the pattern refused them

name: C08 cellLabelValue: the start guard can never fire
why: no punctuation is refused at the start of the id

name: C09 cellLabelValue: the length does not count the quote
why: the id's column of a quoted value is one too far left

name: C10 cellLabelValue: the id keeps the opening quote
why: a quoted value's id starts with its quote

name: C11 cellLabelValue: the run starts at the first character, not past the quote
why: a quoted value's run stops at its own quote

name: C12 cellLabelValue: no ASCII character is a member of the run
to: const end = runEnd(value, from, new Uint8Array(128));
why: no ASCII id is read at all

name: C13 cellLabelValue: a one-character id is refused
why: `a`, `_` and `"a"` define nothing

name: C14 cellLabelValue: an empty id is an answer
why: a lone quote and two quotes answer an empty id

name: C15 cellLabelValue: <= for === on the empty id
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: `runEnd` answers its start or more, never less, so `end <= from` is `end === from`. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: C16 cellLabelValue: the two quotes tested in the other order
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: an `||` of two comparisons of one value does not depend on their order. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: C17 cellLabelValue: the three punctuation marks of the guard in the other order
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: an `||` of three comparisons of one value does not depend on their order. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: N01 narrowLabel: the hash test is inverted
why: every group that begins with a hash is refused

name: N02 narrowLabel: the hash is the wrong character
why: no group begins with the hash it needs

name: N03 narrowLabel: no `fig-`
why: a figure id of a bare group defines nothing

name: N04 narrowLabel: no `tbl-`
why: a table caption's id defines nothing

name: N05 narrowLabel: no `eq-`
why: a display equation's id defines nothing

name: N06 narrowLabel: no `lst-`
why: a listing's id defines nothing

name: N07 narrowLabel: the equation prefix has no dash
why: `#eqa` and `#eq` are read as equation ids

name: N08 narrowLabel: the kind prefix is looked for at the start of the group, not after the hash
why: every group is refused

name: N09 narrowLabel: the run starts at the dash
why: `#fig-` and `#eq-` (a kind prefix with nothing after its dash) answer an id

name: N10 narrowLabel: an empty run is an answer
from: return end === start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
to: return end < start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
why: `#fig-`, `#fig- a` and `#fig-$a` answer a bare kind prefix

name: N11 narrowLabel: the id keeps the hash
from: return end === start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
to: return end === start ? null : content.slice(0, end);
why: every id starts with a hash

name: N12 narrowLabel: the id has no kind prefix
from: return end === start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
to: return end === start ? null : content.slice(start, end);
why: every id is its name alone

name: N13 narrowLabel: a group of another kind answers the empty string
why: `#sec-a` and `#Fig-a` answer an empty id and not null

name: N14 narrowLabel: no ASCII character is a member of the run
to: const end = runEnd(content, start, new Uint8Array(128));
why: no ASCII name is read at all

name: N15 narrowLabel: <= for === on the empty run
from: return end === start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
to: return end <= start ? null : content.slice(1, end);
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: `runEnd` answers its start or more, never less, so `end <= start` is `end === start`. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: N16 narrowLabel: the four kind prefixes in the other order
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: the four kind prefixes begin with four different letters, so at most one of them can follow the hash and the order of the loop does not matter. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: N17 narrowLabel: the hash is tested as a character
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: `content[0] !== "#"` is `content.charCodeAt(0) !== 0x23` (an empty string gives `undefined` and NaN, both unequal to the hash). Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: N18 narrowLabel: the prefix is looked for in a copy of the rest
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: `content.slice(1).startsWith(prefix)` is `content.startsWith(prefix, 1)`. Differential: 2,878,306 strings (the four exhaustive alphabets of the oracle test and 300,000 seeded strings that also hold the CJK letter, the emoji and the kind prefixes) answered the same by this edit and by the committed function, 0 differences.

name: W01 indexLabels: a value that is no label is read
why: every cell label is skipped

name: W02 indexLabels: the column ignores the quote

name: W03 indexLabels: the column one too far right
why: every cell label's column moves

name: W04 indexLabels: the value span ends a character early
why: the last character of every cell label is cut

name: W05 indexLabels: the cell label loses its first character
why: every cell label reads `ig-a`

name: W06 indexLabels: the bare group's content is trimmed
why: `{ #fig-a}` and `{ #eq-n02}` mint labels

name: W07 indexLabels: a group that is no label is read
why: every bare group is skipped

name: W08 indexLabels: the bare group's column is one too far left
from: labels.push({ id: narrowId, kind, line, column: group.start + 2 });
to: labels.push({ id: narrowId, kind, line, column: group.start + 1 });

name: W09 indexLabels: the bare group's id loses its first character
from: labels.push({ id: narrowId, kind, line, column: group.start + 2 });
to: labels.push({ id: narrowId.slice(1), kind, line, column: group.start + 2 });
